summary.text: Vernetta Alston is a Democratic member of the North Carolina House of Representatives who has represented District 29 since 2020 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
She is an attorney and a former Durham City Council member.

paragraphs.text: Vernetta Alston earned a bachelor's degree in political science from North Carolina State University and a law degree from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
Her professional experience includes work as a staff attorney for North Carolina Prisoner Legal Services and the Center for Death Penalty Litigation.
She has also served on Durham's Citizen Advisory Committee, the Durham People's Alliance board, and the University of North Carolina Law Pro Bono Alumni Board.
Alston represented Ward 3 on the Durham City Council from 2017 to 2020.

Governor Roy Cooper appointed her to the state House on April 13, 2020, following the death of Representative MaryAnn Black, and she resigned from the council after being nominated to the legislature.
The Democratic primary for her seat on March 3, 2026, was canceled.
In the 2023-2024 session, Alston was assigned to the Appropriations, Appropriations on Transportation, Environment, Judiciary I, Local Government, and House Transportation committees.
